question: A bird sanctuary had 238 birds. 79 birds arrived during the migration, and then 105 flew away. The sanctuary covers 12 hectares. 13 birds were moved to a zoo, and 175 flew south. Then 24 birds hatched, and 37 more were released into the wild. How many birds are at the sanctuary now?

Two managers compared resource usage. Starting amount: 147 units. Subtracted 59 for current use. Multiplied by 3 for planning. Multiplied by 8 for expansion. Added 6 bonus units. How many units in expanded scenario?

Grower Petra tracked the total pounds of strawberries picked in her field all morning, starting with 27 pounds picked at sunrise. Her farmhand, Solomon, was picking blueberries separately, having gathered 90 pounds, but only Petra's strawberries are tracked here. By mid-morning, a bumper row multiplied her tracked pounds by 7. By midday, a spoiled batch meant 104 pounds had to be discarded from the tracked total. In the afternoon, a second field added 72 more pounds. Converting her tally from pounds to crates for market delivery — a simple unit change — she then set aside 156 crates' worth for a separate order, subtracting it from her tracked total. How many crates were in Petra's tracked total by the end of the afternoon?

A shop had 117 items initially. They multiplied by 8 for stock expansion. They multiplied by 4 for distribution. They removed 43 damaged items. They removed 765 for clearance sale. They added 71 new items. The manager worked 40 hours weekly. How many items remaining?

Two investors tracked a fund balance. Starting with 208 dollars, they added 44 dollars in deposits (252 dollars). The fund was multiplied by 7 through interest (1764 dollars). Market losses reduced by 439 dollars (1325 dollars). The balance was multiplied by 6 (7950 dollars). It was then multiplied by 7 again for annual projection. They said the amount would triple by next year. What was the projected annual amount?

A warehouse received 8 pallets, each stacked with 128 boxes of tiles, and put them all in the loading bay. Over the week the bay shipped out 729 boxes to a builder, 167 boxes to a hardware store, and 118 boxes to a hotel. The boxes still in the bay were then spread equally across 5 shelves. On Friday a delivery of 33 boxes was placed on the top shelf. How many boxes are on the top shelf now?

A baker had 22 loaves. They added 71 loaves. They added 68 loaves. They added 6 loaves. They multiplied by 8 times. The time was minutes to hours. Morning baking, afternoon sales, evening restocking. How many loaves?

A company started with 238 products. They multiplied inventory by 8 times in January. Then by 2 times in February. They shipped 3,215 products to stores. They removed 74 damaged units. What is the final inventory count?

A toy store had 19 action figures in stock. During a sale, they tripled to 57 figures. Then 52 figures were sold to customers. Another 13 figures were damaged and removed. The store restocked and multiplied by 5 for the holiday season. How many action figures does the store have now?

On Monday morning Farmer Hale collected 147 eggs and sold 90 of them at the farm gate. In the afternoon her nephew Theo collected 65 more, though Theo's haul was smaller than Hale's morning collection. In the evening she divided all the eggs on hand into 2 equal crates, keeping one crate for the Saturday stall. Hale sends 6 crates of that same size to the stall every week and keeps that up for 9 weeks. The stall ledger counts eggs in dozens rather than singles, so the clerk converts the numbers at the end. How many eggs in total does Hale send to the stall over those 9 weeks?
A student had 185 items. She added 65. She divided by 2. She removed 103. She removed 12. She removed 6. About 20 items were lost, which is unrelated. How many items?

Fox and Grace track production. They start with 148 units. They multiply by 8 (1184). They multiply by 8 (9472). They add 4 (9476). They lose 6648 (2828). They multiply by 7 (19796). One distractor: competitor made 5000. How much do they produce?

Dana runs a lemonade stall at a market whose till counts in cents, so she converts every hundred cents into a dollar when she writes up her book in dollars. In the morning the stall took 88 dollars, and 58 dollars more came in before noon. In the afternoon it took 67 dollars, and in the evening another 42 dollars. She took exactly that same daily amount on each of the 6 days the market ran. All of that money was shared equally among the 6 members of her co-op, and Raj, another member, received exactly the same share as Dana. Dana then paid 245 dollars for next week's lemons and sugar. How many dollars does Dana have left from her share?
A student had 207 pages. She removed 8 pages. She added 16 more. She removed 106. She removed 60 more. How many pages?

A project budget was 207 dollars. In the morning, 67 dollars were spent. The remaining multiplied by 7. By midday, 11 dollars were added. By afternoon, it multiplied by 8. By evening, 4477 dollars were removed. A distractor: another budget was 95 dollars. How much remained?

A shop starts with 22 items in stock. In the morning, they lose 21 items to sales. By afternoon, they receive 58 items from delivery. By mid-afternoon, they add 10 more items. By evening, they add 72 more items. How many items are in stock at day's end?

A publisher tracked manuscripts. Starting pile: 213 pages. She multiplied by 5 for editing passes. She multiplied by 8 for printing. She added 24 illustrations. She added 79 bonus pages. She multiplied by 7 for distribution units. Morning through evening production. How many units for distribution?

A musician had 193 songs. They multiplied by 9 to calculate practice time. They added 45 songs from new compositions. They added 16 songs from collaborations. They added 35 songs from remixes. How many hours of practice time?

A juice bar begins the day with 96 ounces of fresh orange juice in its large dispenser, or about 3 quarts. A morning rush brings a fresh batch that grows the dispenser's total to 8 times what it was. At noon, the juice is split evenly into 2 separate dispensers, and the story follows just one of those dispensers from here. That dispenser is then split evenly into 2 smaller containers for a catering event, and the story follows just one of those containers from here. An afternoon catering event then uses up 74 ounces from that container. How many ounces of orange juice are in that container now?

A chef had 109 portions. They tripled them. They added 14 portions. They multiplied by 9 times. They removed 1933 portions. David had fewer portions. Maria had more. The total progressed. How many portions?

A single beehive started spring with 28 worker bees in a starter colony. A strong nectar season left the hive with 8 times as many bees. A second growth spurt multiplied the colony by 4. A third growth spurt then multiplied it by 6. Finally, a swarm merger added 48 more bees. A neighboring hive was said to hold about 900 bees, a separate count from this one. How many bees were in this hive in the end?

A dairy had 117 wheels of cheese maturing on its racks. It sold 55 of them to a wholesaler in the spring. A restaurant chain took another 26 wheels in the same month. Every wheel still on the racks was later cut into 7 wedges for the farm shop. The cheesemaker added 30 wedges from an older batch in the cold store and 25 wedges that had come back from a market stall. Each wedge is wrapped in 2 sheets of waxed paper before it goes on sale. How many sheets of waxed paper were needed?

A library had 110 books. They divided by half for classification. They subtracted 1 for a damaged book. They multiplied by 7 for shelf projections. They added 80 books from a donation. They added 19 more books. The annex had 250 books separately. After dividing and subtracting but before multiplication, how many books?

A gardener had 179 seeds. They added 32 seeds of type one. They added 3 seeds of type two. They multiplied by 3 for germination rate. They added 29 seeds that sprouted. How many sprouted seeds were growing?

A cafe had 177 loyalty cards in circulation and issued 68 more in one week. 55 cards were filled up and handed back, and 3 were reported lost. Every card still in circulation carries 4 unused stamp spaces, and the manager Odette counted those spaces. Her colleague Ravi counted fewer spaces on his own set of cards than Odette did. Odette then crossed out 29 spaces that had expired. The cafe records its opening times in minutes even though the door sign gives them in hours. How many stamp spaces did Odette's count come to?
